messages:
Ana: Quick question — seeing route-level flag unexpectedly affecting other model variants in prod canary. Example: project has `enable-kv-cache=true`, route `/short-context` sets `enable-kv-cache=false` and it looks like that false value applied to requests hitting gpt-large too. Is that intended behavior?

Michael: It shouldn't bleed across model variants. Our intended precedence is model > route > project > org (model overrides route, route overrides project). If route sets explicit false it should only affect that route+model combo (unless the override was intentionally wildcarded).

Tara: Can you paste the resolved flag path from the debug logs? For preview routes we sometimes collapse model tags which causes odd resolution mapping.

Ana: Pasted snippet from resolver logs: `/resolve/flags project=proj-eta route=/short-context model=gpt-lite -> resolved: enable-kv-cache=false (route override), quantize=int8 (model override)` — but we then saw `enable-kv-cache=false` on requests routed to `model=gpt-large`.

Ben: That smells like scope key normalization or a cache reuse bug. Two quick suspects: 1) lookup key normalization strips model tag so lookup falls back to route+project only, 2) the flag-resolution cache (LRU) stored a route-scoped resolution and reused it when model var changed. I'll add an extra trace and temp guard.

infra-bot: deploy log: flags-service v2.14.3 rolled by @Ben at 2000502000 :white_check_mark:

Michael: Ben — please file a tiny repro + unit test in `flag-resolver`. We should have an explicit test for "route override doesn't apply to other models unless wildcarded".

Ben: Filing PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2389. Added a guard: when building lookup keys we prefer the most-specific form, e.g.:

```
# lookup order (most specific -> least)
model:flags:proj-eta:/short-context:gpt-large
route:flags:proj-eta:/short-context
project:flags:proj-eta
org:flags
```

Ben: Also instrumented a short-lived metric `flag_resolution.key_format` so we can see if route keys without model are being used incorrectly.

Tara: While we're here, can we add a lint rule to flag overlapping percentage rollouts? Found a case where project had `canary: 5%` and a route had `canary: 100%` which effectively bypassed project guardrails. Something like an `rlint` rule on flag manifests would be useful.

Ana: Strong +1 on the lint. Also product requested the Console show "inherited from" badges in the flag view — makes debugging much easier.

Michael: I'll take Console/API for "inherited from" badges (adding `inherited_from` field on `GET /flags`), Ben owns the resolver PR, Tara will draft the linter rule.

Tara: I'll sketch the lint and a follow-up GH action to fail PRs with dangerous overlap.

Ana: Thanks all. Quick ask — reviewers, can you please take a look at pr/2389 and leave :eyes: before EOD PST? Will follow up if the traces show cache misuse.

Michael: Reviewing now.

Ben: thx, pinged infra-sre to keep an eye on the new metric during the next hour.
